title: Circuit Optimization, Resource Tradeoffs, and Lower Bounds

items.title: Unbounded error time space counting model
items.statement: Use fixed multitape fair-bit probabilistic machines with read-only uncharged input and charged work tapes. Fix either the sequential profile (local heads) or VMW random-access profile (classical input/work-head jumps and maximum-address space); define PrTIME/PrTISP with strict majority and exact oracle answers. The sequential LCH uses at-least-half majority formulas, with tie normalization proved separately.

references.title: Eric Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy
Van Melkebeek and Watson, A Quantum Time-Space Lower Bound for the Counting Hierarchy, Sections 2–3

items.title: Logspace uniform near-linear Cook formula encoding
items.statement: For each fixed deterministic multitape computation of worst-case time T on an input pair (x,y), there is a Boolean formula F(x,y,z) of size O(T log^O(1) T), with each output bit computable in log^O(1) T time and O(log T) space. For fixed x,y, F has a satisfying assignment to z exactly when the computation accepts, and that satisfying z is unique. All variable blocks and the encoding of malformed strings are fixed with the machine.

references.title: Stephen A. Cook, Short Propositional Formulas Represent Nondeterministic Computations
Pippenger and Fischer, Relations among Complexity Measures

items.title: Logspace uniform iterated multiplication threshold circuits
items.statement: This is the local supplier interface for the iterated-product part of constant-depth threshold arithmetic. The input lists m≥1 nonnegative w-bit integers in the explicit binary encoding. The output is their exact product, zero-padded to mw bits. The claimed circuit family has polynomial size in the total input length and constant depth; its circuit description and gate-predecessor predicates are computable in logarithmic space in the input length. This item does not assert a DLOGTIME-uniform multiplication circuit.

references.title: Hesse, Allender, and Barrington, Uniform Threshold Circuits for Division
Eric Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy

items.title: BQTISP Model
items.statement: Define the VMW quantum random-access Turing model: read-only input, classical and quantum work tapes, fixed heads, classical control depending on measurements but not quantum path, coherent input query gates, computable amplitudes, maximum work-head-address space, and bounded-error promise thresholds. Its classical comparison class uses the matching VMW random-access profile.

references.title: Van Melkebeek and Watson, Time-Space Efficient Simulations of Quantum Computation
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Logspace predicates in a fixed linear counting hierarchy level
items.statement: For every language decidable by a deterministic O(log n)-space machine on strings of length n, there is a fixed integer k such that the language lies in LCH_k under the declared sequential or random-access convention. The level may depend on the machine and its uniformity encoding.

references.title: Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy, proof of Lemma 5, step 2

items.title: Bounded-overhead tie normalization for fair-bit machines
items.statement: For a fair-bit probabilistic machine with an explicit time-constructible integer clock $R(n)\ge1$, a machine with no exact $1/2$ acceptance probability can be formed with $O(R(n))$ additional time. It preserves strict-majority membership, and swapping its accept/reject labels decides the complement.

references.title: Van Melkebeek and Watson, A Quantum Time-Space Lower Bound for the Counting Hierarchy, randomization conventions
Eric Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy

items.title: Uniform clocked simulation of encoded probabilistic machines
items.statement: A single clocked probabilistic multitape simulator uniformly simulates descriptions $e$ of length $O(\log n)$ for a time-constructible bound $T(n)\ge n$, preserving each described machine's random-bit distribution and declared input-access profile with time $O(T(n)\,\mathrm{polylog}\,n)$. The fixed-description clocked-simulator bound does not itself state this uniform-in-description conclusion.

references.title: Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy, §2: probabilistic machine and LCH conventions

items.title: Uniform threshold iterated integer arithmetic
items.statement: For $m\ge1$ explicitly listed nonnegative binary integers of at most $w$ bits, iterated sum and product have constant-depth polynomial-size uniform threshold-circuit families over AND/OR/NOT/MAJ. Their exact binary outputs need at most $w+\lceil\log_2m\rceil$ and $mw$ bits, respectively; the claimed uniformity uses the source's logspace-uniform multiplication and DLOGTIME-uniform addition conventions.

references.title: Eric Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy
Hesse, Allender, and Barrington, Uniform Threshold Circuits for Division

items.title: Counting time space to linear hierarchy
items.statement: For constants alpha>1 and 0<beta<1 there exists finite integer tau(alpha,beta) with PrTISP(n^alpha,n^(1−beta)) contained in LCH_tau.

references.title: Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy, Lemma 5
Hesse, Allender, and Barrington, Uniform Threshold Circuits for Division

items.title: Tight majority formula completeness
items.statement: Every LCH1 language reduces to MajSAT, and every LCH2 language reduces to MajMajSAT, with output length n log^O(1)n and each output bit computable in log^O(1)n time and O(log n) space, in the stated input/machine/formula encodings.

references.title: Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy, proof of Theorem 7
Cook, Short propositional formulas represent nondeterministic computations
Pippenger and Fischer, Relations among complexity measures

items.title: Probabilistic polynomial time hierarchy
items.statement: For rational $1\le a<b$ with time-constructible polynomial bounds, $\mathrm{PrTIME}(n^a)$ is properly contained in $\mathrm{PrTIME}(n^b)$ in either one fixed declared access profile. The separation proof requires the uniform-in-description interpreter recorded as [[lem-qc-uniform-probabilistic-clocked-simulation]].

references.title: Eric Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms, probabilistic computation and diagonalization background

items.title: Unbounded error counting time space alternative
items.statement: For every real $d$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $c>1$ such that at least one of the following holds in the sequential machine profile: $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTIME}_{\rm seq}(n^c)$, or $\mathrm{MajSAT}\notin\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm seq}(n^d,n^{1-\varepsilon})$. Formula thresholds are at least-half, and machine acceptance uses strict majority as defined in [[def-qc-unbounded-error-time-space-counting-model]].

references.title: Eric Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Gray-code synthesis of a multiplexed Z rotation
items.statement:
For $k\ge0$ control bits $x\in\{0,1\}^k$ and real angles $\theta_x$, define
$$M_z=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^k}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes R_z(\theta_x),\qquad R_z(t):=\operatorname{diag}(e^{-it/2},e^{it/2}).$$
If $k>0$, this multiplexed rotation has an exact circuit with $2^k$ one-qubit $R_z$ gates and $2^k$ CNOTs; for $k=0$ it is one $R_z$ gate and no CNOT. The CNOT count includes the final parity-restoring CNOT.

references.title: Vivek V. Shende, Stephen S. Bullock, and Igor L. Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits, arXiv:quant-ph/0406176v5
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6

items.title: Basic Clifford T Rewrite
items.statement: On H,T,T†,CNOT words, repeatedly apply a fixed finite rule list such as H²→I, T⁸→I, TT†→I, and CNOT²→I when adjacent gates act on the same wires. Scan a deterministic left-to-right first match; terminate when no rule applies.

references.title: Barenco et al., Elementary gates for quantum computation
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Circuit Resource Composition
items.statement: For circuits placed on a declared common physical register, sequential composition adds gate counts and explicit depths; its width is the declared common-register width. Reusing workspace can make that width the maximum of the component widths only when the alignment and ancilla contracts permit reuse; otherwise all required wires remain allocated. Parallel composition on disjoint registers adds gate counts and widths and has depth equal to the maximum component depth. A clean ancilla is counted as clean only when the complete composed block returns it exactly to zero for every allowed data input.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Unoptimized recursive QSD decomposition and CNOT count
items.statement:
For every $n\ge2$, the recursive cosine-sine/demultiplexing construction gives an exact no-ancilla circuit for any $n$-qubit unitary. At each nonterminal level, split off the first wire as target and let the recursive children act on the remaining contiguous wire interval; the node uses four recursive $(n-1)$-qubit unitaries, one multiplexed $R_y$, and two multiplexed $R_z$ rotations, each with $n-1$ controls. If $c_n$ is the construction's CNOT count, then $c_2\le3$ and
$$c_n\le4c_{n-1}+3\cdot2^{n-1}\quad(n\ge3),\qquad c_n\le\frac9{16}4^n-\frac32 2^n.$$
This is the unoptimized recursive count; it does not include cross-block cancellations or terminal diagonal extraction and makes no compilation-time or finite-precision claim.

references.title: Vivek V. Shende, Stephen S. Bullock, and Igor L. Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits, arXiv:quant-ph/0406176v5
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes, arXiv:1907.09415v6

items.title: Circuit Optimization Task
items.statement: Input a finite circuit over a fixed exact gate alphabet, a declared equality notion (matrix exact, or whole-circuit global-phase equivalence), ancilla policy, and a cost coordinate (count, depth, T-count, width). Output an equivalent circuit with no larger cost; “globally optimal” means no equivalent circuit in the declared model has smaller cost.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Ninefold nearest-neighbor multiplexor routing
items.statement: For the unoptimized recursive QSD circuit, use the contiguous interval layout in which each multiplexed-rotation target is an endpoint, each recursive child acts on the remaining contiguous interval, and each two-qubit terminal block acts on adjacent wires. The line architecture permits both ordered orientations of adjacent CNOT. Replacing each length-$k$ CNOT in a multiplexor by the explicit line-neighbor network below uses at most nine times the original CNOT count. This is an architecture-specific gate-count bound; it asserts no depth bound or arbitrary-layout guarantee.

references.title: Shende, Bullock, and Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits, nearest-neighbor decomposition section

items.title: Basic Rewrite Correct And Terminating
items.statement: Each registered rewrite preserves the exact matrix; the procedure terminates and returns a local normal form relative only to the declared finite rewrite set. It is not claimed globally minimal.

references.title: Barenco et al., Elementary gates for quantum computation
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

items.title: BQTISP To PTISP Simulation
items.statement:
For sufficiently constructible $t,s\ge\log n$, the VMW model satisfies
$$\mathrm{BQTISP}(t,s)\subseteq\mathrm{PrTISP}_{\rm VMW}(t\,\mathrm{polylog}\,t,s+\mathrm{polylog}\,t).$$
The output is an unbounded-error classical probabilistic simulation in the matching VMW random-access profile; it does not assert conversion to the sequential profile.

references.title: Van Melkebeek and Watson, Time-Space Efficient Simulations of Quantum Computation
Dawson and Nielsen, The Solovay–Kitaev Algorithm

items.title: Clean Ancilla Multicontrolled Tradeoff
items.statement: For $m\ge1$ controls, reuse the exact no-workspace $O(m^2)$ and one-clean-bit $O(m)$ constructions from QC11, with total widths $m+1$ and $m+2$ and exact return of the clean bit. These compare construction upper bounds rather than optimal complexities.

references.title: Barenco et al., Elementary gates for quantum computation
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

items.title: Counting Hierarchy Time Space Lower Bound
items.statement: In the VMW random-access quantum Turing model, for every real $d$ and $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $c>1$ such that either $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ has no bounded-error algorithm of time $O(n^c)$, or $\mathrm{MajSAT}$ has no bounded-error algorithm using both time $O(n^d)$ and space $O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$. Consequently, for every $\varepsilon>0$, $\mathrm{MajMajSAT}$ has no bounded-error algorithm with time $n^{1+o(1)}$ and space $O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$.

references.title: Van Melkebeek and Watson, Time-Space Efficient Simulations of Quantum Computation
Eric Allender et al., Time-Space Tradeoffs in the Counting Hierarchy

items.title: Nearest Neighbor CNOT Overhead
items.statement: For the unoptimized recursive QSD circuit in the contiguous interval layout—each multiplexor target is an endpoint, recursive children use the remaining contiguous interval, and terminal two-qubit blocks act on adjacent wires—with both directed orientations of adjacent CNOT allowed, the explicit line routing uses at most nine times the original CNOT count. This is an architecture-specific gate-count bound, not a depth bound or a guarantee for other layouts.

references.title: Shende, Bullock, and Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits, §6
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

items.title: QSD CNOT Upper Bound
items.statement: Reuse QC11 exact QSD: no-ancilla $n$-qubit $U$ needs at most $(23/48)4^n-(3/2)2^n+4/3$ CNOTs. Report one-qubit gates separately; a CNOT count alone is not total classical compilation time. Use $n\ge2$ for this formula; $n\le1$ needs zero CNOT.

references.title: Shende, Bullock, and Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits
Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes

items.title: Generic Circuit Count Lower Bound
items.statement:
Fix a nonempty finite gate alphabet of $A\ge1$ gates, each of arity at most $k$ with $1\le k\le3$, and count circuits on $n\ge1$ classical input wires with zero-initialized ancillas and one designated measured output bit. No additional classical acceptance predicate is free. For a gate budget $C\ge n$, put $W=n+kC+1$. After deleting unused ancillas, every such circuit has at most $W$ wires, and there are at most
$$W\sum_{j=0}^{C}(AW^k)^j=\exp(O(C\log C))$$
output-designated gate-list descriptions. Each description computes at most one Boolean function with success probability at least $2/3$ on every input. Hence, for all sufficiently large $n$, at least $99\%$ of Boolean functions on $n$ bits require $\Omega(2^n/n)$ gates. If arbitrary classical postprocessing is allowed, its circuit or description cost must be included; otherwise this conclusion need not hold.

references.title: Ronald de Wolf, Quantum Computing: Lecture Notes
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms

title: Circuit Optimization, Resource Tradeoffs, and Lower Bounds — Examples

items.title: Two-qubit QSD CNOT upper-bound instance
items.statement: Substituting n=2 into the stated no-ancilla QSD count gives (23/48)·16−(3/2)·4+4/3=3 CNOTs, with one-qubit gates counted separately.

references.title: Shende, Bullock, and Markov, Synthesis of Quantum Logic Circuits
Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
